solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Colour endless in a divine English novel (4,4)

indicatorNotes.endless: the colour loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: the shortened colour sits inside the divine

blocks.note: DD = Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman

annotation.surface: A literary critic muses on the colours in a devout English novel.
annotation.walkthrough: A divine is a clergyman, and DD is the degree after his name. Adam Bede is George Eliot's first novel.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Eliot's first full-length book, published in 1859, is one instance of the category.

entries.clue: Help mounted soldiers cutting spring migration (8)

indicatorNotes.mounted: in a down clue, going up turns the word over
indicatorNotes.cutting: the soldiers cut into the spring

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring

annotation.surface: Mounted troops arrive to help with a seasonal migration in spring.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mounted soldiers" looks like cavalry, but "mounted" belongs to "Help": in a down entry it lifts AID to read DIA.
annotation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the scattering or migration of a people from their homeland.

entries.clue: Folk performer, crafty poet leading reindeer (6,6)

blocks.note: William Morris, Arts and Crafts designer and poet

annotation.surface: A cunning poet heads a herd of reindeer at a folk festival.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crafty" here means of the Arts and Crafts movement, not cunning: William Morris led it and wrote poetry. A morris dancer performs a traditional English folk dance.
annotation.definitionFit: A morris dancer performs traditional English folk dances with bells and sticks.

entries.clue: Nutty green apple finally prepared for cake (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of apple
indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are made ready, rearranged

annotation.surface: A baker prepares green apples and nuts for a cake.
annotation.walkthrough: "Nutty green" reads as two adjectives describing an apple; in fact it is a noun phrase, a green who is nuts about the environment.
annotation.definitionFit: Green as a noun is an environmentalist, and nutty adds the fanaticism the slang freak carries.

entries.clue: Just for Latinists, this with others has to go round (7)

indicatorNotes.for Latinists: the words are to be put into Latin
indicatorNotes.has to go round: the Latin for others surrounds the Latin for this

blocks.note: et al, Latin for and others

annotation.surface: A pedantic note on Latin grammar about words that must surround others.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces must be translated into Latin: hic is this and et al. is and others.
annotation.definitionFit: Just and ethical both mean morally right.

entries.clue: Complaint NHS department’s well able to explain? (6)

blocks.note: ENT = ear, nose and throat; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: Can the NHS department that handles this complaint explain itself properly?
annotation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. The question mark flags a looser definition: a fluent speaker is well able to explain.
annotation.definitionFit: A fluent speaker expresses themselves easily, so is well able to explain.

entries.clue: Duke in good health carrying spades (4)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the word for good health holds the spades

annotation.surface: A healthy duke goes about carrying garden spades.
annotation.walkthrough: "Duke" looks like a nobleman, but dukes is slang for fists, as in "put up your dukes".
annotation.definitionFit: Dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist.

entries.clue: Plot involving alien laser beam accidentally revealed? (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: the plot takes in the alien and the beam

blocks.note: a flower bed is a garden plot

annotation.surface: A science-fiction plot in which an alien's laser beam gives something away.
annotation.walkthrough: "Plot" reads as a story line; it is a garden bed. The question mark allows betrayed in its sense of gave away unintentionally.
annotation.definitionFit: Betrayed can mean unintentionally showed, as a blush betrays embarrassment.

entries.clue: Maybe 501s with shirt put outside to air (8)

indicatorNotes.put outside: the shirt goes around the jeans

blocks.note: 501s are a style of Levi's jeans

annotation.surface: Jeans and a shirt are hung outside to air.
annotation.walkthrough: "To air" sounds like drying laundry; here air means broadcast.
annotation.definitionFit: Air in the broadcasting sense, as in a programme going out on air, is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Young swimmer Henry’s widow (4)

blocks.note: a young salmon, before it goes to sea
Henry VIII's sixth wife, Catherine, outlived him

annotation.surface: A young swimmer turns out to be the widow of someone called Henry.
annotation.walkthrough: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and the only one to survive him.
annotation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon; Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's widow.

entries.clue: Chilled environment in wild for rare tiger (12)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild means out of control, and letters out of control will not keep their order

annotation.surface: A zoo keeps a rare tiger in a cool enclosure in the wild.
annotation.walkthrough: "Environment" suggests a habitat for the tiger; the chilled environment is simply a fridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description rather than a synonym: the fridge is literally a cold space that surrounds whatever is kept in it.

entries.clue: Fools in America delinquent once hit (12)

blocks.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s young tearaway

annotation.surface: A news item about foolish American young offenders who once struck someone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fools" is plural, so two ASSes. A Ted was a Teddy boy, a British youth of the 1950s in Edwardian-style dress, a byword for delinquency, hence "once".
annotation.definitionFit: A mob hit is a killing, so hit means assassinated.

entries.clue: Dessert timid sort swallows slowly at first (6)

indicatorNotes.swallows: the timid sort takes the letter inside
indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of slowly

annotation.surface: A shy diner eats pudding slowly at first.
annotation.walkthrough: Calling a shy person a mouse is the usual crossword shorthand for timid sort.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the light whipped chocolate or fruit pudding is one kind of sweet course.

entries.clue: Blakey for one is to strive for creative skill (8)

annotation.surface: A musician named Blakey works hard at his craft.
annotation.walkthrough: Art Blakey was an American jazz drummer; British readers may also think of Blakey from the sitcom On the Buses, but only Art works.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names the skill an artist brings to the work.

entries.clue: Nothing stops Kelvin, a debauchee, in pub activity (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: the nothing plugs the gap inside the debauchee

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute man

annotation.surface: Nothing can halt Kelvin, a hard-living man, when he gets going at the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: "Kelvin" reads as a man's name, but it is the temperature unit, K.
annotation.definitionFit: Karaoke, singing along to backing tracks, is a common pub activity.

entries.clue: Almost do away with range of knowledge on New York City (8)

indicatorNotes.Almost: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

annotation.surface: An attempt to wipe out the sum of knowledge about New York City.
annotation.walkthrough: "New York City" looks like one unit; the definition is City alone, and Kilkenny is a city in Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: Kilkenny is a city in the south-east of Ireland.

entries.clue: Adult struck — struck with shame (7)

annotation.surface: An adult is hit, and then feels thoroughly ashamed.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated "struck" does two jobs: first a physical blow, then the start of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means disconcerted and embarrassed, the feeling of being hit by shame.

entries.clue: Bishop in argument about new Victorian poet (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the bishop comes in at the front of the argument
indicatorNotes.about: the argument goes round the new

annotation.surface: A bishop is caught up in a dispute about a new Victorian poet.
annotation.walkthrough: Rowing, rhyming with cow, is British for having a row. Robert Browning was a leading Victorian poet.
annotation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was one of the great Victorian poets.

entries.clue: Place abnormally loaded with hidden gold (2,6)

indicatorNotes.hidden: the gold is concealed inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A place unusually rich, stuffed with buried gold.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the legendary city, rich with gold. OR as gold comes from heraldry.
annotation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary place of gold sought by explorers in South America.

entries.clue: Shock where old hand guzzles gallon (7)

indicatorNotes.guzzles: the old hand swallows the gallon

blocks.note: an old stager is a veteran

annotation.surface: It's shocking how much an old man can drink.
annotation.walkthrough: "Old hand" is one unit: an old stager, a veteran. Stagger means shock or astound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: news that makes you reel astonishes you.

entries.clue: Jousting weapon returned to lake for knight (8)

annotation.surface: A knight's jousting lance is returned to the lake, as Excalibur was.
annotation.walkthrough: "Returned" looks as if it acts on the weapon, as Excalibur was returned to the lake, but it acts on what follows. Fittingly, the knight was known as Lancelot du Lac.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the best-known knight of the Round Table.

entries.clue: Irrigation of Algarve at regular intervals over time (6)

indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: letters taken at evenly spaced gaps, here every second one, starting from the second

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: Farmers in the Algarve water their fields regularly over the years.
annotation.walkthrough: "Over" places AGE after the extracted letters. Lavage is a medical washing out, as of a wound or the stomach.
annotation.definitionFit: Lavage is washing out a body cavity, a medical irrigation.

entries.clue: Spaniards here competed in scoreless draw (6)

annotation.surface: A Spanish football team plays out a goalless draw.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spaniards" suggests a team, but the definition is a place where Spaniards live: Oviedo, a city in northern Spain.
annotation.definitionFit: Oviedo is a Spanish city, a place Spaniards are found.

entries.clue: Show without Tarzan struggling to entertain Virginia and Georgia (12)

indicatorNotes.to entertain: the rearranged Tarzan holds the two states

blocks.note: ex = without, as in ex dividend

annotation.surface: A show goes ahead without its Tarzan, who is busy hosting American guests.
annotation.walkthrough: Ex as a preposition means without, as in ex works price.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with extra colour: the word means a spectacular, lavishly staged entertainment.

entries.clue: American not eating in land around Lomé (4)

blocks.note: Lomé is the capital of a small West African country

annotation.surface: An American traveller in West Africa who won't eat in the local restaurants.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration is (4), so TO GO reads as one word. Americans order food to go where Britons order takeaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Americans say to go for food not eaten in; Togo is the country whose capital is Lomé.

entries.clue: Son leaves belt in corner (4)

indicatorNotes.leaves: the son goes out of the word

annotation.surface: A boy slips out of his belt while in the corner.
annotation.walkthrough: "Corner" looks like a noun; it is the verb, to trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to pin someone where they cannot escape.

entries.clue: Excited seeing leg — not small — in flimsy robe (8)

indicatorNotes.not small: remove S, the abbreviation for small

annotation.surface: Someone is aroused at the sight of a leg in a sheer dressing gown.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is racy, and the answer belongs in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A negligee is a flimsy, often sheer, dressing gown.

entries.clue: Dance party taking place next to European capital (8)

indicatorNotes.next to: the party and place follow the capital

annotation.surface: A dance party is being held near a European capital.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dance party" looks like one phrase; Dance is the definition and party is DO. A rigadoon is a lively old dance for couples.
annotation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively Baroque dance in duple time.
